flows.description: Editor-driven session creation, prompts and permission responses.
Reads daemon.token and the pinned certificate to authenticate.
Authenticated API traffic carrying the bearer token and conversation content.
Unattended run start with the job's stored mode and workdir.
Prompt, file content and tool results sent to a cloud model.
web_fetch/web_search requests and retrieved page content.
MCP tool invocation and wrapped results.
Prompt and tool results sent to a local model.
Per-call capability classification and allow/ask/deny decision.
Model-requested shell commands and their bounded output.
Tool listing and invocation against a third-party server.
MCP client-driven session creation and prompt turns.
Scanner image execution with --network none and a workspace mount.
Prompts, slash commands and approval decisions.
Browser session against the daemon's embedded SPA.
docker/podman run with hardening flags and workspace mount.
Snapshot writes before mutating tool calls and restores on rewind.
Job registration, listing and lifecycle.
Auth token and TLS key material generation and reuse.
Turn execution, event streaming and approval round-trips.
Scan requests and aggregated findings.
Conversation, trace and cost persistence.
Trust grant lookup and recording, keyed by directory and fingerprint.
Session, message and approval API calls.
Page-token mint and exchange, then bearer-authenticated API calls and SSE.

threats.title: Abuse — Long parallel tool rounds produce repeated approval prompts, training the operator to approve without reading
threats.description: Long parallel tool rounds produce repeated approval prompts, training the operator to approve without reading — approval fatigue that converts a deliberate gate into a rubber stamp.
threats.mitigation: Batch related approvals with a single reviewable summary; surface the resolved argv rather than the raw command string.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A pathological model response (a single multi-megabyte line, or dense wide-glyph content) stalls the render...
threats.description: A pathological model response (a single multi-megabyte line, or dense wide-glyph content) stalls the render loop and makes the UI unresponsive.
threats.mitigation: Bound per-render line length and total buffered output in the TUI view layer.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Model output rendered to the terminal includes file contents the agent read, which may contain credentials
threats.description: Model output rendered to the terminal includes file contents the agent read, which may contain credentials; no redaction is applied on the display path.
threats.mitigation: Apply `internal/redact` to rendered tool results, not only to shared transcripts.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Terminal scrollback and any terminal-emulator logging retain secrets that appeared in agent output after th...
threats.description: Terminal scrollback and any terminal-emulator logging retain secrets that appeared in agent output after the session ends.
threats.mitigation: Document the scrollback exposure; offer a "no secrets to screen" posture that redacts by default.

threats.title: Repudiation — An approval decision shown and accepted in the TUI leaves no independent record on the client side
threats.description: An approval decision shown and accepted in the TUI leaves no independent record on the client side; the only trace is whatever the daemon persists.
threats.mitigation: Enable the `internal/hooks` audit hook so `PolicyDecision` records are written for every gate outcome.

threats.title: Tampering — Repository or model content rendered in the terminal carries ANSI/OSC escape sequences that rewrite the ter...
threats.description: Repository or model content rendered in the terminal carries ANSI/OSC escape sequences that rewrite the terminal title, inject keystrokes, or hide text from the operator reviewing an approval.
threats.mitigation: `internal/termsafe` (`StripControlSeqs`, `StripDangerousSeqs`) strips control sequences before rendering.

threats.title: Abuse — Any local process running as the operator can read `daemon.token` and use this same client library to drive...
threats.description: Any local process running as the operator can read `daemon.token` and use this same client library to drive full agent turns — the client is not a privilege boundary.
threats.mitigation: Document explicitly that same-user local processes are inside the trust boundary; consider per-client tokens with scopes.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The bearer token is held in process memory and attached to every request
threats.description: The bearer token is held in process memory and attached to every request; a crash dump or debugger attach on the client process exposes it.
threats.mitigation: Zero the token buffer after use where practical; document that a same-user debugger defeats this.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Client-side request/response logging would persist full conversation content including any secrets present...
threats.description: Client-side request/response logging would persist full conversation content including any secrets present in tool results.
threats.mitigation: `internal/redact` is applied to persisted/shared output (`security.redact_secrets: true` by default).

threats.title: Spoofing — The client pins whatever certificate is present at `<DataDir>/daemon.crt`
threats.description: The client pins whatever certificate is present at `<DataDir>/daemon.crt`; a same-user process that writes that file before the client first reads it makes the client trust an impersonating listener.
threats.mitigation: Apply `fsguard.RestrictToOwner` to `daemon.crt` as well as `daemon.token`, and record a pin fingerprint the client can compare.

threats.title: Tampering — Deleting `daemon.crt`/`daemon.key` causes silent regeneration on next daemon start, changing the pin with n...
threats.description: Deleting `daemon.crt`/`daemon.key` causes silent regeneration on next daemon start, changing the pin with no operator-visible signal.
threats.mitigation: Log loudly on regeneration and require an explicit acknowledgement when a previously-seen pin changes.

threats.title: Abuse — An operator exposing the UI through an SSH tunnel or reverse proxy meets a self-signed-certificate warning...
threats.description: An operator exposing the UI through an SSH tunnel or reverse proxy meets a self-signed-certificate warning and is conditioned to click through it, defeating the pin.
threats.mitigation: The CLI calls the warning out explicitly when TLS is on; document a supported operator-supplied `cert_file`/`key_file` path for tunnelled access.

threats.title: Denial of Service — `GET /ui` is exempt from `authMiddleware` and mints a page token per load
threats.description: `GET /ui` is exempt from `authMiddleware` and mints a page token per load; once 1024 unexpired tokens are outstanding, `mintPageToken` refuses and the operator's own UI will not load.
threats.mitigation: The cap is a deliberate memory bound (refuse rather than evict). Add per-source-address minting throttling so a flood cannot deny the operator's own load.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A hostile page frames or embeds `/ui` to drive privileged actions with the operator's session (clickjacking...
threats.description: A hostile page frames or embeds `/ui` to drive privileged actions with the operator's session (clickjacking / cross-origin reads).
threats.mitigation: `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`, and `originMiddleware` rejecting non-loopback `Origin` headers.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The CSRF cookie is minted without `Secure` when the request did not arrive over TLS, so on a plaintext depl...
threats.description: The CSRF cookie is minted without `Secure` when the request did not arrive over TLS, so on a plaintext deployment it can travel over a non-TLS hop.
threats.mitigation: `server.tls.enabled` defaults to `true`, so `r.TLS != nil` and `Secure` is set on the default deployment; `trust_proxy_headers` covers the reverse-proxy case.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The real daemon token is delivered into browser JavaScript memory, where any script-injection defect in the...
threats.description: The real daemon token is delivered into browser JavaScript memory, where any script-injection defect in the SPA (or a malicious browser extension with host access) can read and exfiltrate it.
threats.mitigation: Keep the daemon token out of JS entirely by proxying calls through a cookie-authenticated session; the CSP (`default-src 'self'`) reduces but does not remove the exposure.

threats.title: Spoofing — Any local process that can reach the loopback port calls `GET /ui`, reads the page token out of the respons...
threats.description: Any local process that can reach the loopback port calls `GET /ui`, reads the page token out of the response body and the CSRF nonce out of the `Set-Cookie` header, and redeems both at `/auth/exchange` for the real daemon token — the double-submit binding stops hostile *web pages*, not raw HTTP clients.
threats.mitigation: Documented as accepted residual risk in the code (`uiCSRFCookieName` doc comment). Bind the exchange to an operator-visible confirmation, or require the real token for the first `/ui` load when one is available.

threats.title: Tampering — The SPA is served from a committed `dist/` embedded at build time
threats.description: The SPA is served from a committed `dist/` embedded at build time; drift between `frontend/src` and `dist/` is caught only by the web-UI drift check in `ci.yml`, whose push/PR triggers are commented out.
threats.mitigation: Re-enable the CI triggers, or add the drift check to a workflow that still runs on push.

threats.title: Abuse — An editor plugin can drive continuous unattended turns
threats.description: An editor plugin can drive continuous unattended turns — legitimate functionality used to run the agent without the operator's attention.
threats.mitigation: Surface an editor-driven-run indicator and apply the same run budgets used for interactive sessions.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — The permission mode for an ACP session is chosen by the client at `session/new`, so an editor plugin can re...
threats.description: The permission mode for an ACP session is chosen by the client at `session/new`, so an editor plugin can request a more permissive posture than the operator's interactive default.
threats.mitigation: Clamp client-requested modes to a configured ceiling, as `mcp_server.default_mode` now does for the MCP path.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Prompt content, file contents and tool results traverse stdio in cleartext to the editor process.
threats.description: Prompt content, file contents and tool results traverse stdio in cleartext to the editor process.
threats.mitigation: Same-host, same-user pipe; no network exposure and no additional confidentiality boundary to defend.

threats.title: Repudiation — Permission responses arrive as `session/request_permission` replies from the editor with no evidence a huma...
threats.description: Permission responses arrive as `session/request_permission` replies from the editor with no evidence a human saw the prompt; an editor plugin can auto-answer.
threats.mitigation: Record the approval channel (`acp`) alongside the decision so a transcript distinguishes editor-answered from human-answered approvals.

threats.title: Spoofing — The peer on the other end of stdio is whatever process the editor launched
threats.description: The peer on the other end of stdio is whatever process the editor launched; `handleAuthenticate` verifies a shared token but cannot distinguish the editor from anything else that inherited the pipe.
threats.mitigation: Document the stdio trust assumption; the token check bounds accidental, not deliberate, misuse by a same-user process.

threats.title: Abuse — `mcp_server.auto_approve_tools` can be widened to auto-approve execute-capable tools, turning the MCP surfa...
threats.description: `mcp_server.auto_approve_tools` can be widened to auto-approve execute-capable tools, turning the MCP surface into unattended command execution.
threats.mitigation: `mcp_server.auto_approve` defaults to `false`, and auto-approval is now per-tool rather than one undiscriminated yes.

threats.title: Denial of Service — An MCP client can start many concurrent runs and consume the daemon's global run slots, starving the operat...
threats.description: An MCP client can start many concurrent runs and consume the daemon's global run slots, starving the operator's interactive session.
threats.mitigation: `server.max_concurrent_runs` defaults to 10 and `server.max_run_duration_sec` to 1800, both explicitly sized to bound a lower-trust caller like `mcp-serve`.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — `callPrompt` accepts any `session_id` verbatim, so an authenticated MCP client can post a turn into an inte...
threats.description: `callPrompt` accepts any `session_id` verbatim, so an authenticated MCP client can post a turn into an interactive `auto`-mode session and inherit that session's mode, persona, workdir and `additional_roots` — a workspace the MCP path could never have created for itself.
threats.mitigation: Filed as **P80.1**; needs a recorded session origin filtered server-side.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — The `mcp_server.default_mode` clamp binds only sessions this server creates
threats.description: The `mcp_server.default_mode` clamp binds only sessions this server creates; a borrowed session carries whatever mode it already had, so the clamp is bypassed by reuse.
threats.mitigation: Same fix as T05.E1 — the clamp is only meaningful once session ownership is enforced.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — `aegis_list_sessions` proxies `Backend.ListSessions`, which is the daemon's `store.List`
threats.description: `aegis_list_sessions` proxies `Backend.ListSessions`, which is the daemon's `store.List` — every session on the daemon, including titles and working directories of sessions created interactively.
threats.mitigation: Filter the listing to sessions this server instance created, or to a recorded session origin.

threats.title: Repudiation — A turn injected into a session the MCP client did not create is recorded indistinguishably from a turn the...
threats.description: A turn injected into a session the MCP client did not create is recorded indistinguishably from a turn the operator typed in the TUI.
threats.mitigation: Record message origin (`mcp`, `acp`, `tui`, `cron`) on every persisted turn.

threats.title: Spoofing — Anything able to write to this subprocess's stdin drives full agent turns
threats.description: Anything able to write to this subprocess's stdin drives full agent turns; the `authenticate` method is the only barrier and the pipe is inherited from whoever launched the process.
threats.mitigation: Documented in the package (`internal/mcpserver/server.go:84`). Treat launch of `mcp-serve` as equivalent to granting agent access.

threats.title: Abuse — Any token holder can create a session in `auto` mode with `auto_approve_exec`, then drive unattended host c...
threats.description: Any token holder can create a session in `auto` mode with `auto_approve_exec`, then drive unattended host command execution through a legitimate API.
threats.mitigation: Clamp API-requested modes to a configured ceiling the same way the MCP path now does.

threats.title: Denial of Service — The unauthenticated `/ui` route mints page-token entries
threats.description: The unauthenticated `/ui` route mints page-token entries; at `maxPageTokens` the daemon refuses to mint and the web UI stops loading for everyone.
threats.mitigation: Refusing rather than evicting is deliberate; add per-address throttling ahead of the cap.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Repeated invalid authentication engages a process-wide lockout window that could wedge the operator's own c...
threats.description: Repeated invalid authentication engages a process-wide lockout window that could wedge the operator's own client out of its own daemon.
threats.mitigation: The token is checked *before* the lockout window and a valid token is served throughout it, so a local guesser cannot lock out the legitimate holder.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Setting `server.allow_remote: true` converts a loopback service into a network service whose entire access...
threats.description: Setting `server.allow_remote: true` converts a loopback service into a network service whose entire access control is one static bearer token with no TLS client authentication and no per-user identity.
threats.mitigation: The bind is refused without the flag and a startup WARN is emitted; document that remote exposure requires an external authenticating proxy.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — `/healthz` is exempt from authentication, letting any local process confirm the daemon's presence and readi...
threats.description: `/healthz` is exempt from authentication, letting any local process confirm the daemon's presence and readiness without credentials.
threats.mitigation: Minimal by design; keep the response free of version, workspace or session detail.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — SSE event streams carry full conversation content, tool inputs and tool results to whichever client holds t...
threats.description: SSE event streams carry full conversation content, tool inputs and tool results to whichever client holds the token.
threats.mitigation: `server.tls.enabled: true` by default encrypts the loopback hop against a local packet-capture adversary.

threats.title: Repudiation — Successful privileged operations
threats.description: Successful privileged operations — config PATCHes, session deletion, prune, harden — produce no dedicated audit record; only failed authentication is logged, and only one attempt in five.
threats.mitigation: Emit a structured audit event for every state-changing endpoint.

threats.title: Repudiation — The `internal/hooks` audit sink is opt-in, so a default deployment retains no tamper-evident record of tool...
threats.description: The `internal/hooks` audit sink is opt-in, so a default deployment retains no tamper-evident record of tool executions or policy decisions.
threats.mitigation: Enable a default-on audit log under the data directory with owner-only permissions.

threats.title: Spoofing — Authentication is possession of a single long-lived bearer token on disk
threats.description: Authentication is possession of a single long-lived bearer token on disk; every local process running as the operator is indistinguishable from the operator's own client.
threats.mitigation: Constant-time compare and lockout are in place; add token rotation and per-client scoped credentials.

threats.title: Tampering — `PATCH /config/sandbox`, `/config/security`, `/config/skills` and `/config/cost` mutate security-relevant r...
threats.description: `PATCH /config/sandbox`, `/config/security`, `/config/skills` and `/config/cost` mutate security-relevant runtime settings over the API with nothing beyond the bearer token — including the sandbox backend that confines command execution.
threats.mitigation: Require an explicit interactive confirmation (or a separate privileged token) for endpoints that weaken isolation.

threats.title: Tampering — `server.session_workdir_allowlist` is documented as ignored on the default loopback bind, so any token hold...
threats.description: `server.session_workdir_allowlist` is documented as ignored on the default loopback bind, so any token holder can create a session rooted at any directory the daemon can read.
threats.mitigation: Apply the allowlist unconditionally, or gate non-default workdirs behind the workspace-trust prompt.

threats.title: Abuse — Loop-detection exemptions (`PollExempter`, `SignatureTransparent`) hide calls or arguments from the repetit...
threats.description: Loop-detection exemptions (`PollExempter`, `SignatureTransparent`) hide calls or arguments from the repetition breaker, which a model could exploit to loop indefinitely.
threats.mitigation: Tests keep both exemption sets narrow and disjoint, and `SignatureTransparent` is barred from covering model-chosen search queries.

threats.title: Abuse — An injected instruction or a looping model drives sustained metered spend against a cloud provider using en...
threats.description: An injected instruction or a looping model drives sustained metered spend against a cloud provider using entirely legitimate functionality.
threats.mitigation: Depends on T07.D1 — without a default budget there is no ceiling on this abuse.

threats.title: Denial of Service — The primary spend and length bounds
threats.description: The primary spend and length bounds — `cost.budget_usd`, `cost.max_tokens_per_run`, `cost.session_cap_usd`, `cost.daily_cap_usd` — all default to `0`, meaning unlimited.
threats.mitigation: Ship non-zero defaults, or refuse to start a cloud-provider session with no bound set.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A long-running tool call stalls a turn indefinitely, holding a run slot and the model server.
threats.description: A long-running tool call stalls a turn indefinitely, holding a run slot and the model server.
threats.mitigation: `cost.max_turn_stall` defaults to 900s and is the one bound that covers tool execution; `TestToolTimeoutsStayUnderTheStallBound` enumerates per-call timeouts.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A per-call capability computed against the wrong root would classify a call as a read when it executes else...
threats.description: A per-call capability computed against the wrong root would classify a call as a read when it executes elsewhere, widening the effective capability across the approval round-trip.
threats.mitigation: `tool.CapabilityOverrider` takes a context and classifies against `effectiveRoot`; `tool.WithCapabilityMemo` makes the verdict single-valued for the gate, scheduler and bookkeeping.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Handing a sub-agent, debate role or session the parent `Registry` rather than a clone would let session-sco...
threats.description: Handing a sub-agent, debate role or session the parent `Registry` rather than a clone would let session-scoped tools escape their session.
threats.mitigation: `Registry.Clone()` overlays exposure decisions and routes clone-local registration to an overlay; both directions are pinned by tests.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Every file the agent reads, plus the repo map and tool results, is placed in a provider request
threats.description: Every file the agent reads, plus the repo map and tool results, is placed in a provider request; the redaction pass protects shared and persisted transcripts, not the outbound provider payload.
threats.mitigation: Apply `internal/redact` (or an explicit allowlist prompt) to provider requests when the provider is a non-loopback cloud endpoint.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Truncated tool-result remainders spill to `<workspace>/.aegis/spill/` as plaintext files that outlive the t...
threats.description: Truncated tool-result remainders spill to `<workspace>/.aegis/spill/` as plaintext files that outlive the turn and are reachable by `read_file`.
threats.mitigation: Write spill files with owner-only permissions and reap them at session end.

threats.title: Repudiation — A tool call interrupted mid-flight could be reported to the model as "not run" when it had in fact started,...
threats.description: A tool call interrupted mid-flight could be reported to the model as "not run" when it had in fact started, losing the record of a side effect.
threats.mitigation: `repairOrphanedToolUses` reports a started call as *possibly* completed, never as not run (P65.1); `Engine.startedTools` tracks the set.

threats.title: Spoofing — The prose tool-call shim (`internal/provider/prosetoolcall.go`, `internal/toolshim`) parses tool calls out...
threats.description: The prose tool-call shim (`internal/provider/prosetoolcall.go`, `internal/toolshim`) parses tool calls out of free-form model text, so content the model merely *quotes* — from a fetched page or an MCP result — can be promoted into a real tool call.
threats.mitigation: Keep the shim off by default (`provider.tool_call_shim: off`) and never parse tool calls out of content that arrived inside an untrusted-content wrapper.

threats.title: Tampering — Indirect prompt injection: instructions embedded in fetched web content, MCP results or repository files st...
threats.description: Indirect prompt injection: instructions embedded in fetched web content, MCP results or repository files steer the model into issuing tool calls the operator never asked for.
threats.mitigation: `internal/trust` wraps such content and scans it heuristically, but the wrapper is advisory to the model — it constrains nothing mechanically.

threats.title: Tampering — In a parallel tool round, read/network calls take no lock and are deliberately not held off by a concurrent...
threats.description: In a parallel tool round, read/network calls take no lock and are deliberately not held off by a concurrent write; only same-`path` calls are ordered, and the dependency graph keys on the literal `"path"` input field, so a `shell` call and a `read_file` are never ordered against each other.
threats.mitigation: Documented design (P8.6). Extend the dependency graph to cover shell commands whose argv contains a path also used by a concurrent write.

threats.title: Abuse — `permission.plan_mode_shell_reads` defaults to `true`, trading plan mode's hard guarantee for the ergonomic...
threats.description: `permission.plan_mode_shell_reads` defaults to `true`, trading plan mode's hard guarantee for the ergonomics of `shell("git log")` — precisely the posture an operator selects when reviewing an untrusted repository.
threats.mitigation: Default the flag to `false` for workspaces that have not been granted trust.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — `Gate.Check` consults `tool.EffectiveCapability` *before* `Policy.Decide`, so a call downgraded by the clas...
threats.description: `Gate.Check` consults `tool.EffectiveCapability` *before* `Policy.Decide`, so a call downgraded by the classifier is allowed silently in every mode — including plan mode, whose documented guarantee is that no commands run at all.
threats.mitigation: `permission.plan_mode_shell_reads: false` makes the guarantee unconditional; it is not the default.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A bare `permission.New` at an `engine.New` call site yields the mode gate alone
threats.description: A bare `permission.New` at an `engine.New` call site yields the mode gate alone — no rules, contextual policy, persona-tool or scope layer (the P66.13 bypass class).
threats.mitigation: `internal/enginecfg.BuildGate` is the single constructor and `TestEveryEngineCallSiteDecidesItsGate` fails any new `engine.New` that neither uses it nor justifies its absence.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A persona's `tools:` list is advisory
threats.description: A persona's `tools:` list is advisory — it prompts and warns but never enforces — so a persona documented as read-only can still issue write and execute calls.
threats.mitigation: Documented in `docs/personas.md`. Offer an enforcing mode for personas used as a containment boundary.

threats.title: Repudiation — Gate decisions are surfaced through `Audit.PolicyDecision`, which only records anything when the audit hook...
threats.description: Gate decisions are surfaced through `Audit.PolicyDecision`, which only records anything when the audit hook is configured — off in a default deployment.
threats.mitigation: Make the policy-decision log default-on.

threats.title: Tampering — `classifyShellCommand` is roughly 1,129 lines of hand-written argument parsing across 40+ commands and thre...
threats.description: `classifyShellCommand` is roughly 1,129 lines of hand-written argument parsing across 40+ commands and three shell dialects; any parsing defect makes a mutating or escaping command classify as a read. Two such defects (an unexpanded `~`, an unconfined `argv[0]`) have already shipped and been fixed.
threats.mitigation: `FuzzClassifyShellCommand` states the invariant (a `CapRead` verdict implies nothing outside root is touched and no binary from inside root is executed); keep the fuzz corpus growing with every fixed case.

threats.title: Abuse — A server controls its own tool descriptions, which are injected into the model's context and can be written...
threats.description: A server controls its own tool descriptions, which are injected into the model's context and can be written to induce the model to call that tool with sensitive arguments.
threats.mitigation: Wrap MCP-supplied tool descriptions in the same untrusted-content marker already applied to MCP results.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A hanging or slow MCP server holds a tool-call slot and stalls the turn.
threats.description: A hanging or slow MCP server holds a tool-call slot and stalls the turn.
threats.mitigation: Per-call timeouts are enumerated by `TestToolTimeoutsStayUnderTheStallBound` and kept under the 900s turn-stall bound.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A tool newly advertised by a server after the session started becomes callable without any fresh operator a...
threats.description: A tool newly advertised by a server after the session started becomes callable without any fresh operator approval of that server's expanded surface.
threats.mitigation: Require re-approval when a server's advertised tool set grows, not just when its schemas change.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Tool arguments constructed by the model can carry workspace file contents or credentials to a third-party M...
threats.description: Tool arguments constructed by the model can carry workspace file contents or credentials to a third-party MCP server.
threats.mitigation: `warnOutboundSecrets` logs a warning but does not block; add a redaction or refusal path for arguments matching `internal/redact` classes.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — MCP server credentials live in `.aegis/.env`, which is a project-controlled file.
threats.description: MCP server credentials live in `.aegis/.env`, which is a project-controlled file.
threats.mitigation: `.aegis/.env` is read only in a trusted workspace, may not set `AEGIS_*` keys, and is ACL-restricted on Windows via `fsguard`.

threats.title: Spoofing — A stdio MCP server's identity is the configured command path
threats.description: A stdio MCP server's identity is the configured command path; a replaced or shimmed binary on `PATH` is indistinguishable from the intended server.
threats.mitigation: Resolve configured server commands to absolute paths and record a binary digest at first use.

threats.title: Tampering — A server can replace a tool's schema mid-session via `tools/list_changed`, changing what an already-approve...
threats.description: A server can replace a tool's schema mid-session via `tools/list_changed`, changing what an already-approved tool name does.
threats.mitigation: Registry clones share one `toolTable` so a parent re-registration reaches existing clones, and stale schema caches are discarded when the parent version moves.

threats.title: Abuse — Cron is a persistence mechanism: an attacker who obtains the bearer token once can register a recurring job...
threats.description: Cron is a persistence mechanism: an attacker who obtains the bearer token once can register a recurring job that keeps running after the token is rotated.
threats.mitigation: Show registered jobs prominently at daemon start and require re-confirmation of jobs created outside an interactive session.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Overlapping schedules start concurrent runs that consume the daemon's global run slots.
threats.description: Overlapping schedules start concurrent runs that consume the daemon's global run slots.
threats.mitigation: `server.max_concurrent_runs` (default 10) and `server.max_run_duration_sec` (default 1800) bound both the count and the duration.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A job created in `auto` mode auto-approves execute-capable tool calls on every future firing, indefinitely,...
threats.description: A job created in `auto` mode auto-approves execute-capable tool calls on every future firing, indefinitely, with no operator in the loop.
threats.mitigation: Refuse `auto` mode for scheduled jobs unless the sandbox backend is a real isolation backend, mirroring `allow_unsandboxed_auto_exec`.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A job whose working directory differs from the daemon's workspace would be classified against the wrong roo...
threats.description: A job whose working directory differs from the daemon's workspace would be classified against the wrong root, mis-scoping every capability decision.
threats.mitigation: `tool.CapabilityOverrider` classifies against `effectiveRoot`; cron jobs were the case that motivated it.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — A scheduled run reads workspace files and sends them to the configured provider with nobody watching, so an...
threats.description: A scheduled run reads workspace files and sends them to the configured provider with nobody watching, so an exfiltration path opened by injection runs unobserved.
threats.mitigation: Require an explicit per-job acknowledgement when the job's provider is a non-loopback cloud endpoint.

threats.title: Repudiation — Output and side effects of an unattended run are attributed to no human, and are recorded the same way an i...
threats.description: Output and side effects of an unattended run are attributed to no human, and are recorded the same way an interactive turn is.
threats.mitigation: Stamp a `cron` origin on every persisted turn and every audit record produced by a scheduled run.

threats.title: Tampering — A stored job's prompt and configuration are executed later with no operator present
threats.description: A stored job's prompt and configuration are executed later with no operator present; a job row modified in the cron SQLite store changes what runs.
threats.mitigation: Restrict the cron database to owner-only, and re-display a job's full definition before each first run after modification.

threats.title: Abuse — With `sandbox.network` enabled, the shell tool becomes a general-purpose network client that bypasses the S...
threats.description: With `sandbox.network` enabled, the shell tool becomes a general-purpose network client that bypasses the SSRF blocklist enforced on `web_fetch`.
threats.mitigation: `sandbox.network` defaults to `false`; when enabled, apply an egress policy to the container rather than leaving it unrestricted.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A runaway command exhausts host memory, CPU or process table, starving the model server the agent depends on.
threats.description: A runaway command exhausts host memory, CPU or process table, starving the model server the agent depends on.
threats.mitigation: `sandbox.limits` defaults to 4G memory, 2 CPUs and 1024 PIDs per container.

threats.title: Denial of Service — The `local` backend applies none of those limits
threats.description: The `local` backend applies none of those limits — a fork bomb or memory hog runs unbounded on the host.
threats.mitigation: Apply OS-level resource limits (job objects on Windows, rlimits/cgroups on POSIX) to locally-executed commands.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — `SelectSandbox` cascades container → OS → `local` and emits only a startup WARN, so a Windows host with no...
threats.description: `SelectSandbox` cascades container → OS → `local` and emits only a startup WARN, so a Windows host with no container runtime silently executes every agent command unconfined.
threats.mitigation: `sandbox.strict` makes the fallback fatal but is not the default; make strict the default and require an explicit opt-out.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — `auto_approve_exec` combined with the unsandboxed local backend is unattended remote code execution on the...
threats.description: `auto_approve_exec` combined with the unsandboxed local backend is unattended remote code execution on the host.
threats.mitigation: The daemon refuses to start on that combination unless `permission.allow_unsandboxed_auto_exec` is set explicitly.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — The persistent per-workspace container keeps state between commands for the session TTL, so a command that...
threats.description: The persistent per-workspace container keeps state between commands for the session TTL, so a command that plants a shim or modifies `PATH` inside the container affects every later command in the session.
threats.mitigation: Persistence is on by default (`sandbox.persistent: true`); document the retained-state model and offer a per-command reset.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The spawned process inherits the daemon's environment minus a denylist (`DefaultStripEnv` plus configured n...
threats.description: The spawned process inherits the daemon's environment minus a denylist (`DefaultStripEnv` plus configured names), so any secret-bearing variable not on the list is visible to the command.
threats.mitigation: Invert to an allowlist: pass only the variables a command legitimately needs.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The workspace mount exposes everything under the root to the command, including `.aegis/.env` and any crede...
threats.description: The workspace mount exposes everything under the root to the command, including `.aegis/.env` and any credential files the developer keeps in-tree.
threats.mitigation: Exclude `.aegis/.env` and configured secret paths from the mount.

threats.title: Repudiation — Executed commands are recorded only through the opt-in audit hook, so a default deployment has no durable r...
threats.description: Executed commands are recorded only through the opt-in audit hook, so a default deployment has no durable record of what the agent ran.
threats.mitigation: Default-on command audit log under the data directory.

threats.title: Tampering — The `local` backend runs the model's command directly on the host with the operator's full privileges and n...
threats.description: The `local` backend runs the model's command directly on the host with the operator's full privileges and no filesystem confinement beyond the tool-level path checks.
threats.mitigation: Reached only when neither a container runtime nor an OS sandbox is available; make that state a hard failure under a `sandbox.strict` default rather than a WARN.

threats.title: Tampering — The container backend bind-mounts the workspace read-write, so a command inside the sandbox can rewrite any...
threats.description: The container backend bind-mounts the workspace read-write, so a command inside the sandbox can rewrite any workspace file including `.aegis/config.yaml` and project skills.
threats.mitigation: Mount read-only for read-classified commands, and route writes through the checkpointed tool path.

threats.title: Abuse — `recon_scan` auto-authorizes every loopback and RFC1918 target with no allowlist entry, so a model-issued c...
threats.description: `recon_scan` auto-authorizes every loopback and RFC1918 target with no allowlist entry, so a model-issued call can port-scan and template-scan the operator's home or corporate LAN.
threats.mitigation: `security.dast.allow_active` defaults to `false` for aggressive checks, but passive nmap/nuclei sweeps of private space need no configuration at all.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A rogue or looping scanner floods stdout and exhausts daemon heap.
threats.description: A rogue or looping scanner floods stdout and exhausts daemon heap.
threats.mitigation: `execbound.go` caps retained scanner output at 64 MiB while still draining the pipe to completion.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A scanner container with both the workspace mounted and network access could exfiltrate source.
threats.description: A scanner container with both the workspace mounted and network access could exfiltrate source.
threats.mitigation: The multiscanner runs `--network none` with the workspace mounted; `aegis-netscanner` runs with network and never a workspace mount; `update-db` is the only networked run of the former.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Scan reports embed source excerpts and dependency inventories and are written into the workspace where they...
threats.description: Scan reports embed source excerpts and dependency inventories and are written into the workspace where they may be committed.
threats.mitigation: `internal/security/redact.go` scrubs findings; add the report path to a generated `.gitignore` entry.

threats.title: Spoofing — Scanner image identity is asserted by a mutable tag rather than a digest, so a compromised registry or a lo...
threats.description: Scanner image identity is asserted by a mutable tag rather than a digest, so a compromised registry or a local image rebuild substitutes a different scanner.
threats.mitigation: `aegis security verify-image` exists; make verification a precondition of a scan run rather than a separate command.

threats.title: Tampering — A scanner that fails partway reports a confident but wrong finding count, which an operator would read as "...
threats.description: A scanner that fails partway reports a confident but wrong finding count, which an operator would read as "clean".
threats.mitigation: gosec is the one two-phase tool and a failed warm phase aborts the scan rather than reporting a count.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Concurrent runs contend on a single SQLite file and can pile up on lock waits.
threats.description: Concurrent runs contend on a single SQLite file and can pile up on lock waits.
threats.mitigation: `journal_mode=WAL` plus a 5s `busy_timeout` applied per connection through the DSN.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Full conversation content
threats.description: Full conversation content — including file contents and any secrets the agent read — is persisted unencrypted and retained indefinitely.
threats.mitigation: Offer at-rest encryption keyed to the OS credential store, and a retention policy that prunes old sessions by default.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — `sqlitestore.Open` creates the parent directory `0o700` but the database file itself is created by the driv...
threats.description: `sqlitestore.Open` creates the parent directory `0o700` but the database file itself is created by the driver with default permissions and no `fsguard.RestrictToOwner` call, so on Windows it inherits the parent ACL rather than an owner-only one.
threats.mitigation: Apply `fsguard.RestrictToOwner` to the database file (and its `-wal`/`-shm` companions) as `daemon.token` already does.

threats.title: Repudiation — Trace records are the closest thing to an audit trail and they are freely mutable, so they cannot support a...
threats.description: Trace records are the closest thing to an audit trail and they are freely mutable, so they cannot support a repudiation claim.
threats.mitigation: Keep security-relevant events in a separate append-only log rather than the same mutable database.

threats.title: Tampering — Any process running as the operator can edit the SQLite file directly, rewriting conversation history and t...
threats.description: Any process running as the operator can edit the SQLite file directly, rewriting conversation history and trace records with no integrity check on read.
threats.mitigation: Add a per-record MAC or an append-only trace log so history tampering is detectable.

threats.title: Abuse — `/rewind` is a legitimate feature that silently reverts files, so an injected instruction can use it to und...
threats.description: `/rewind` is a legitimate feature that silently reverts files, so an injected instruction can use it to undo a reviewer's edits or erase evidence of a prior tool call.
threats.mitigation: Require explicit confirmation for a rewind that would discard changes made outside the agent's own tool calls.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Per-turn snapshots of a large workspace grow without a documented bound and can fill the disk.
threats.description: Per-turn snapshots of a large workspace grow without a documented bound and can fill the disk.
threats.mitigation: Cap total snapshot bytes per session and evict oldest first.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Snapshots contain complete copies of workspace files, including any secrets present at snapshot time, and p...
threats.description: Snapshots contain complete copies of workspace files, including any secrets present at snapshot time, and persist after the session that created them.
threats.mitigation: Reap snapshots with the session, and apply owner-only permissions to the snapshot directory.

threats.title: Tampering — A modified snapshot is restored over live workspace files on rewind, so tampering with the store becomes ta...
threats.description: A modified snapshot is restored over live workspace files on rewind, so tampering with the store becomes tampering with the working tree.
threats.mitigation: Record a content digest per snapshot and verify it before restore.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — The fingerprint deliberately excludes `.aegis/.env`, so a project can change the secrets loaded into the da...
threats.description: The fingerprint deliberately excludes `.aegis/.env`, so a project can change the secrets loaded into the daemon's environment without invalidating an existing trust grant.
threats.mitigation: Documented as a deliberate hole in `internal/config/fingerprint.go`; the load-order constraint that motivates it should be revisited so the file can be covered.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A grant written before fingerprints existed has an empty `Fingerprint` and would otherwise match any config...
threats.description: A grant written before fingerprints existed has an empty `Fingerprint` and would otherwise match any configuration.
threats.mitigation: `Store.Check` treats an empty fingerprint as a pre-P66.25 grant and re-prompts once.

threats.title: Repudiation — An entry records only `TrustedAt` and the fingerprint
threats.description: An entry records only `TrustedAt` and the fingerprint — not who granted it or through which interface — so an inserted grant is indistinguishable from an operator decision.
threats.mitigation: Record the granting interface and process identity alongside each entry.

threats.title: Tampering — The grant file is written `0o600` inside a `0o700` directory but carries no integrity protection, so a same...
threats.description: The grant file is written `0o600` inside a `0o700` directory but carries no integrity protection, so a same-user process can insert a grant for any directory and suppress the trust prompt.
threats.mitigation: Apply `fsguard.RestrictToOwner` to the store file and sign the entry set with a key held in the OS credential store.

threats.title: Denial of Service — An unwritable or full data directory prevents token generation and blocks daemon start.
threats.description: An unwritable or full data directory prevents token generation and blocks daemon start.
threats.mitigation: `generateAndWriteToken` returns the error and `ListenAndServe` refuses to start with an empty token, failing closed.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — A world-readable token file would expose the daemon credential to every account on a shared host.
threats.description: A world-readable token file would expose the daemon credential to every account on a shared host.
threats.mitigation: Written `0o600` and then hardened by `fsguard.RestrictToOwner`, which applies a real non-inherited owner-only ACL on Windows where the mode bit is cosmetic.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The token never rotates for the life of the file, so a credential captured once (backup, snapshot, screen s...
threats.description: The token never rotates for the life of the file, so a credential captured once (backup, snapshot, screen share) stays valid indefinitely.
threats.mitigation: Rotate on daemon restart, or on an interval, with clients re-reading the file.

threats.title: Spoofing — Possession of `daemon.token` is the entire identity model
threats.description: Possession of `daemon.token` is the entire identity model — there is no binding to a process, user session or client certificate.
threats.mitigation: Add per-client tokens issued on an operator-confirmed handshake so a stolen credential is scoped and revocable.

threats.title: Tampering — Deleting `daemon.crt`/`daemon.key` makes the daemon regenerate them on next start, silently changing the ce...
threats.description: Deleting `daemon.crt`/`daemon.key` makes the daemon regenerate them on next start, silently changing the certificate every pinned client trusts.
threats.mitigation: Treat regeneration of an existing pin as an event requiring explicit operator acknowledgement.

threats.title: Abuse — Legitimate agent behaviour drives unbounded metered spend, since every `cost.*` cap defaults to `0`.
threats.description: Legitimate agent behaviour drives unbounded metered spend, since every `cost.*` cap defaults to `0`.
threats.mitigation: Ship non-zero `cost.session_cap_usd`/`cost.daily_cap_usd` defaults for cloud providers.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Vendor rate limiting, quota exhaustion or an outage stalls every run.
threats.description: Vendor rate limiting, quota exhaustion or an outage stalls every run.
threats.mitigation: Retry, failover and admission-control decorators wrap the adapter (`internal/provider/retry.go`, `failover.go`, `admission.go`).

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Source code, configuration and any secrets present in read files leave the operator's machine for a third p...
threats.description: Source code, configuration and any secrets present in read files leave the operator's machine for a third party under that vendor's retention terms.
threats.mitigation: Apply `internal/redact` to outbound provider payloads when the endpoint is not loopback, and surface a per-session indicator of what has been sent.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — A `base_url` on plaintext HTTP would send the API key in the clear.
threats.description: A `base_url` on plaintext HTTP would send the API key in the clear.
threats.mitigation: `validateBaseURL` refuses outright when the scheme is `http`, the host is non-loopback and a real API key would be attached.

threats.title: Repudiation — There is no local, tamper-evident record of exactly what payload left the host for the vendor, so a later d...
threats.description: There is no local, tamper-evident record of exactly what payload left the host for the vendor, so a later data-exposure question cannot be answered from the machine.
threats.mitigation: Log a hash and byte count of each outbound provider payload to the audit sink.

threats.title: Spoofing — A `provider.base_url` override pointed at an attacker-controlled HTTPS host receives every request includin...
threats.description: A `provider.base_url` override pointed at an attacker-controlled HTTPS host receives every request including the API key; the override is warned about, not refused.
threats.mitigation: `validateBaseURL` warns when a cloud provider's default host is overridden. Escalate to a confirmation prompt, or treat the override as a security-relevant config key frozen under workspace trust.

threats.title: Tampering — The model's response is trusted to shape tool calls
threats.description: The model's response is trusted to shape tool calls; a compromised or substituted endpoint controls what the agent does next.
threats.mitigation: Keep destructive tool calls behind operator approval regardless of provider, which the default `build` mode does for execute-capable tools.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Model load, eviction, or a `num_ctx` mismatch between the Modelfile and the daemon's plan stalls or degrade...
threats.description: Model load, eviction, or a `num_ctx` mismatch between the Modelfile and the daemon's plan stalls or degrades every run.
threats.mitigation: The `num_ctx` decorator and the persisted per-model capability cache (`internal/modelcaps`) detect and adapt; the turn-stall bound reclaims a wedged run.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A pulled model file carries no signature, so a poisoned or backdoored model steers tool calls while appeari...
threats.description: A pulled model file carries no signature, so a poisoned or backdoored model steers tool calls while appearing to be the model the operator selected.
threats.mitigation: Model provenance is the model host's and Ollama's responsibility; Aegis can only record the digest it was served.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Prompts containing workspace file contents traverse that same plaintext loopback hop.
threats.description: Prompts containing workspace file contents traverse that same plaintext loopback hop.
threats.mitigation: Same remediation as T18.T; the daemon's own listener already solved this with pinned TLS.

threats.title: Spoofing — Ollama listens on loopback with no authentication, so any local process that binds the port first
threats.description: Ollama listens on loopback with no authentication, so any local process that binds the port first — or wins a restart race — answers as the model and dictates the agent's tool calls.
threats.mitigation: Support a shared secret or Unix-socket path for the local provider, and record the endpoint's identity across restarts.

threats.title: Tampering — Completions traverse plaintext loopback HTTP and can be observed or modified by a local process with packet...
threats.description: Completions traverse plaintext loopback HTTP and can be observed or modified by a local process with packet-capture privilege.
threats.mitigation: Allow TLS to a local provider endpoint, and prefer a filesystem socket where the platform supports it.

threats.title: Abuse — A server writes its tool descriptions specifically to induce the model to call it with sensitive arguments,...
threats.description: A server writes its tool descriptions specifically to induce the model to call it with sensitive arguments, using a legitimate protocol feature as a social-engineering channel against the model.
threats.mitigation: Wrap server-supplied descriptions in the untrusted-content marker already applied to their results.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A hanging server stalls the tool round it participates in.
threats.description: A hanging server stalls the tool round it participates in.
threats.mitigation: Per-call timeouts are enumerated and kept below the turn-stall bound.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A server can advertise a tool whose name shadows or resembles a built-in, so the model calls the external o...
threats.description: A server can advertise a tool whose name shadows or resembles a built-in, so the model calls the external one believing it is calling the harness.
threats.mitigation: Namespace MCP tool names on exposure and reject collisions with built-in names.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The model chooses tool arguments, so an injected instruction can move workspace file contents into an argum...
threats.description: The model chooses tool arguments, so an injected instruction can move workspace file contents into an argument sent to the server.
threats.mitigation: `warnOutboundSecrets` warns only; add refusal for arguments matching known secret classes.

threats.title: Spoofing — A stdio server is authenticated only by the fact that the configured command started
threats.description: A stdio server is authenticated only by the fact that the configured command started; an HTTP server is authenticated only by TLS to a configured URL.
threats.mitigation: Pin an absolute command path and a binary digest for stdio servers; require a pinned certificate or token for HTTP servers.

threats.title: Tampering — Tool results are attacker-controlled text placed directly into the model's context
threats.description: Tool results are attacker-controlled text placed directly into the model's context — the primary indirect prompt-injection vector in the system.
threats.mitigation: `wrapUntrusted` always applies a provenance marker and `trust.ScanForInjection` annotates hits, but neither constrains the model mechanically.

threats.title: Tampering — `tools/list_changed` lets a server swap a tool's schema and semantics after the operator has already approv...
threats.description: `tools/list_changed` lets a server swap a tool's schema and semantics after the operator has already approved calls to that name.
threats.mitigation: Re-prompt on a semantic change to an approved tool, not only on the first approval.

threats.title: Abuse — `web_fetch` is a legitimate feature that doubles as an exfiltration channel: an injected instruction encode...
threats.description: `web_fetch` is a legitimate feature that doubles as an exfiltration channel: an injected instruction encodes file content into a URL the agent then fetches.
threats.mitigation: Combine the T20.I redaction with an operator-visible egress log of every fetched URL.

threats.title: Denial of Service — A slow or very large response ties up the fetch path.
threats.description: A slow or very large response ties up the fetch path.
threats.mitigation: Bounded retries with `webBackoff`, a response-size limit via `defaultFetchLimit`, and per-call timeouts under the stall bound.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — SSRF: a fetch to a loopback or private address reaches the operator's Ollama, the Aegis daemon itself, or a...
threats.description: SSRF: a fetch to a loopback or private address reaches the operator's Ollama, the Aegis daemon itself, or a cloud metadata endpoint.
threats.mitigation: `netblock.SafeDialer` blocks `0.0.0.0/8`, RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local, multicast, reserved space and the NAT64 prefix, and `CheckRedirect` re-validates every redirect hop.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The model chooses the URL, so workspace-derived data can be encoded into the request path or query string a...
threats.description: The model chooses the URL, so workspace-derived data can be encoded into the request path or query string and observed by the destination.
threats.mitigation: Apply `internal/redact` classes to outbound URLs and refuse fetches whose URL contains material matching a secret pattern.

threats.title: Spoofing — Search results are scraped from DuckDuckGo/Marginalia HTML and carry no origin authentication beyond transp...
threats.description: Search results are scraped from DuckDuckGo/Marginalia HTML and carry no origin authentication beyond transport TLS; a challenge page or a poisoned result set is parsed as authoritative.
threats.mitigation: `looksLikeDDGChallenge`/`looksLikeMarginaliaChallenge` detect interstitials; surface parse-confidence to the model rather than presenting scraped results as facts.

threats.title: Tampering — Fetched HTML is converted to text and enters model context, making any page the model visits an injection v...
threats.description: Fetched HTML is converted to text and enters model context, making any page the model visits an injection vector.
threats.mitigation: `trust.Wrap` marks the content and `ScanForInjection` annotates hits, including zero-width-obfuscated payloads; the marker is advisory.

threats.title: Denial of Service — If the runtime is unavailable or a container fails to start, `SelectSandbox` degrades to a weaker backend r...
threats.description: If the runtime is unavailable or a container fails to start, `SelectSandbox` degrades to a weaker backend rather than failing the command, so a runtime outage becomes a silent loss of isolation.
threats.mitigation: Make the degradation fatal by default (`sandbox.strict`) so an outage is a visible failure.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — On Linux, membership of the `docker` group is equivalent to host root, so any process able to drive the run...
threats.description: On Linux, membership of the `docker` group is equivalent to host root, so any process able to drive the runtime — including the sandboxed command if the socket is reachable — can escape to the host.
threats.mitigation: Docker's group-equals-root model is the runtime's, not Aegis's; prefer rootless Podman and never mount the socket into a container.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — A container running with default capabilities and privilege escalation enabled weakens the isolation the sa...
threats.description: A container running with default capabilities and privilege escalation enabled weakens the isolation the sandbox exists to provide.
threats.mitigation: `OCIHardeningFlags` applies `--cap-drop=ALL` and `--security-opt=no-new-privileges` to every run, alongside memory, CPU and PID limits.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — The workspace bind mount makes every file under the root readable inside the container, including files the...
threats.description: The workspace bind mount makes every file under the root readable inside the container, including files the specific command had no need to see.
threats.mitigation: Mount only the paths a command's classified argv requires.

threats.title: Tampering — `sandbox.image` defaults to the mutable tag `ubuntu:22.04`
threats.description: `sandbox.image` defaults to the mutable tag `ubuntu:22.04`; the image behind that tag can change between runs, and scanner images are likewise referenced by tag.
threats.mitigation: Pin images by digest and record the resolved digest in the scan/session record.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection is marked but not constrained
External MCP servers are trusted on configuration alone
Configuration endpoints can disable command isolation with only the bearer token
The web UI hands the real daemon token to browser JavaScript
Outbound provider payloads and tool arguments are never redacted
`provider.base_url` override redirects credentials and model control on a warning only
The local model endpoint is unauthenticated plaintext HTTP on loopback
`web_fetch` is an unreviewed egress channel
Session working-directory allowlist is not enforced on the default bind
The container workspace mount exposes the whole workspace to every command
Build, test, vulnerability and lint gates no longer run on push or pull request
Release artifacts ship without checksums, signatures or provenance
Container and scanner images are referenced by mutable tag
No default audit trail for privileged operations, policy decisions or executed commands
All cost and token budgets default to unlimited
The unauthenticated `/ui` mint can be flooded to deny the operator's own UI
Web UI assets are served from a committed `dist/` whose drift check no longer runs
The self-signed certificate warning conditions operators to click through
`/healthz` discloses daemon presence without authentication
Plan mode's read-only guarantee rests on a 1,129-line shell classifier
An MCP client can enumerate and post turns into sessions it did not create
Command isolation silently degrades to unsandboxed host execution
Scheduled jobs run unattended in whatever mode they were created with
Conversation history and checkpoints persist secrets unencrypted
The daemon token and pinned certificate never rotate and are not integrity-checked
Sandboxed commands inherit the daemon environment minus a denylist
Workspace trust grants are unauthenticated local state and exclude `.aegis/.env`
Prose tool-call parsing can promote quoted untrusted text into real tool calls
`recon_scan` auto-authorizes every loopback and RFC1918 target
Parallel tool rounds do not order shell commands against concurrent writes
Checkpoint growth is unbounded and `/rewind` can silently discard non-agent changes
Scan reports embed source excerpts into the workspace
The TUI render path is unbounded and repeated approvals invite blanket approval
